name: tofu calamari
instructions:
Iberian/spanish tapas plates built on crispy baked tofu — no variants, it's all one valid plate: tofu calamari with whatever's on hand from the spanish condiment shelf.

=== THE PLATE (ALL OF IT VALID, MIX FREELY) ===

- CRISPY BAKED TOFU: super firm or extra firm (the kind that doesn't need pressing — see notes), HAND-SHREDDED (fractal edges crisp better than cube faces — source: Nisha), tossed in potato starch (or cornstarch) with a heavy hand of ONION + GARLIC POWDER, salt, pepper, vegetable oil. Bake at ~425°F until crisp and browned.
- [[sauce-andalouse]] and/or [[romesco]] as the dips, plus [[tartar-sauce]] and [[relish]] — both primary; the calamari register wants its fried-seafood condiments.
- RAW PEPPERS (bell, chopped bite-sized) and RAW CELERY — both firm, stable dipping agents (see notes).
- PITA CHIPS (or corn chips) for the dips between tofu bites.
- FREEZER FRIES — bake alongside the tofu; they share the oven and the dips.
- LEMON JUICE over the hot tofu — for bite; always some. THE CITRUS PAIRING RULE: LEMON goes with the andalouse/tartar side of the plate, LIME with the romesco side (lime is secondary overall).
- Optional: honey drizzle on the hot tofu; a cold cream cheese glob as a second dip.

EATING IT: build-your-own tapas — dip a shred, scoop some romesco, squeeze citrus, repeat.
notes:
=== UNRETIRED + CONSOLIDATED (SEPTEMBER 2026) ===

The lineage: italian-asian-tofu-plate → tofu-cube-protein-plate (retired in the east asian pruning, gochujang variant deleted) → baked-tofu-plates → crispy-spanish-tofu-plates → TOFU CALAMARI. The variants collapsed: romesco+chips and sauce andalouse aren't separate plates, they're the same IBERIAN/SPANISH TAPAS register — it's all valid on one plate.

=== WHY THIS RECIPE EXISTS — MAKING THE PROTEIN BINGE PALATABLE ===

Eating a LOT of tofu protein in one sitting without it being a chore. The crispy shreds are efficient (one sheet pan, no flipping) and the tapas accompaniments — dips, raw peppers, chips, citrus — keep the binge interesting.

=== THE TOFU — RULES ===

- SUPER FIRM / EXTRA FIRM — the kind that DOESN'T NEED PRESSING. That's what the crumble-with-garlic/onion-powder technique works best with. REGULAR FIRM TOFU ISN'T IDEAL for this crispy variant — firm/pressed tofu is better for other things, like the tofu tikka meal ([[tikka-masala]]).
- SHRED BY HAND, don't cube: fractal edges crisp better than clean cube faces (source: Nisha). Keep shreds large — big pieces read as the meal.
- HEAVY SEASONING HAND: potato starch (crispest) or cornstarch + lots of onion/garlic powder + salt + pepper. Under-seasoned tofu flattens the plate.
- OIL SO THE STARCH CRISPS; hot oven (~425°F). Under-crisped reads soggy/boiled.

=== WANT TO TRY — BAKED POLENTA CUBES ON THE PLATE ===

BAKED POLENTA cubes ([[polenta]] — hardened, cubed, oil-sprayed, baked at 425°F) might pair well with this plate. Same oven temperature as the tofu. Untested.

=== WANT TO TRY — PANKO IN THE STARCH/SEASONING TOSS ===

PANKO mixed into the potato starch + onion/garlic powder toss. It will taste good — the open question is whether you can NAIVELY bread it that way (everything mixed all at once): panko may not adhere to the shreds without a wet step the way the starch does.

=== THE CALAMARI READ ===

Crispy starch crust + bright citrus + spiced mayo ([[sauce-andalouse]]) lands on the fried-calamari register — tofu as the squid, andalouse as the aioli. LEMON is non-optional; the calamari read collapses without acid. THE PAIRING RULE: LEMON pairs with [[sauce-andalouse]] and [[tartar-sauce]]; LIME pairs with [[romesco]]. Lime is secondary overall — lemon is the default citrus of the plate.

=== RAW VEGETABLES — FIRM DIPPERS ONLY ===

RAW CELERY alongside the bell peppers — I like them together because both are FIRM and thus STABLE DIPPING AGENTS. The rule that follows: cauliflower, asparagus, and broccoli have never worked on plates like this — THEY DON'T DIP (florets crumble and shed, spears don't scoop). Firm, flat-ish, rigid raw vegetables only.

=== THE DIPS ===

- [[sauce-andalouse]]: the spiced red-pepper mayo — the aioli slot.
- [[romesco]]: the smoky-nutty dip; honey-drizzled tofu + romesco covers the sweet-savory-smoky triangle.
- Cold CREAM CHEESE glob optional as a contrast dip — keep it cold for the temperature play against the hot tofu.
Both dips on one plate is fine — that's the tapas logic.

=== SIBLING RECIPES ===

- [[sauce-andalouse]] / [[romesco]]: the dips, both standalone recipes.
- [[italian-stuffed-bell-peppers]]: variant B uses the same seasoned-crisped-tofu technique in crumble form.
- [[mcfadden-cucumber-salad]]: the fresh side this plate wants in summer.
- [[mexican-tofu-fritters]]: the MEXICAN version of this plate — same tofu engine, cornmeal/masa + chili powder in the coat, mexican spread instead of tapas.
